options: A study of cognitive processes & behavior
questions.explanation: Psychology is the scientific study of mind (cognitive processes) and behavior. It is not merely an art of living or a study of the body, which belongs to biology and physiology.

questions.q: A broad field of study that explores a variety of questions about thoughts, feelings and actions is ____?
questions.explanation: Psychology specifically investigates thoughts, feelings and actions of individuals. Social science is a broader umbrella that also covers economics, sociology and politics, so it is less precise.

questions.q: Learning has been a central topic of research in ____.
questions.explanation: Learning, as a relatively permanent change in behavior or knowledge due to experience, has been a core research area in psychology since the work of Ebbinghaus, Pavlov, Thorndike and others.
Psychology comes from the Greek words psyche (mind or soul) and logos (study). Hence psychology originally meant the study of the mind or soul.

questions.q: The ____ of learning focuses on how people learn.
questions.explanation: The psychology of learning studies the processes by which people acquire, retain and use new knowledge, skills and behaviors.

questions.q: To help people to function effectively and fulfill their own unique potential" is the aim of ____?
questions.explanation: Humanistic psychology (Maslow, Rogers) emphasizes personal growth, free will and self-actualization, i.e., helping people fulfill their unique potential.

questions.q: Psychology is not an independent science, but dependent on other fields.
questions.explanation: Psychology is an independent science with its own subject matter and methods, formally established when Wundt founded the first psychology laboratory in 1879. It draws on and interacts with other fields but is not dependent on them.

questions.q: The study of changes in an individual's behavior during his/her lifetime is called ____.
questions.explanation: Developmental psychology studies how behavior, cognition and emotion change across the lifespan, from infancy through old age.

questions.q: The study of differences and similarities in the behavior of animals of different species is called ____.
questions.explanation: Comparative psychology compares behavior across species to understand evolutionary and functional similarities and differences. Cultural psychology compares human cultures, not species.
Humans are highly capable learners; learning occurs throughout life through experience, practice, observation and instruction.
